stem:
Pranav has two ropes of lengths $36\,\mathrm{m}$ and $48\,\mathrm{m}$. He wants to cut both into pieces of the same whole-number length, using the largest possible piece length with no rope left over.

Which two claims correctly state what he should find and why?

options.text: Find a common multiple of $36$ and $48$.
Find the highest common factor of $36$ and $48$.
The largest equal piece length that divides both $36$ and $48$ with no remainder is that highest common factor.
Any common factor of $36$ and $48$ is enough, even when a larger one also fits.

teacher.key_rationale: Largest equal piece with no remainder is the HCF of 36 and 48. A common multiple answers a different question; any common factor may be too small.
